summary: The Bahamas' Department of Immigration lists the countries whose citizens' Bahamian visa requirements are waived for visits of no more than three or eight months, as each individual agreement may dictate, and the countries whose citizens must apply for and obtain Bahamian visas before attempting entry. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs publishes its own lists of who does and does not need a visa. Travellers who are not citizens or legal residents must present a completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card at the border.

processing.text: The standard processing time for an eVISA is 7-10 business days

validityDays.text: A single entry visa is valid for one entry only to The Bahamas with the time frame of three (3) months.

entries.text: A single entry visa is valid for one entry only to The Bahamas with the time frame of three (3) months.

extendable.text: If you want to stay beyond the period granted, you can apply for a visitor extension before the time granted expires and is subject to the discretion of the Department of Immigration.

name.text: Self-Sponsored Visitor Visa is issued to persons travelling to the Bahamas for the purpose of leisure.

method.text: Welcome to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Online Portal for Electronic Entry Visas (EEV).

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Extension of Stay

alsoStatedOn.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival (visitor extension)

extendable.text: An extension on visitors’ stay may be granted to applicant who qualify.

name.text: the Government of The Bahamas has introduced a non-refundable application processing fee of $200.00 for the Extension of Stay application.

method.text: Please note that this process in no way nullifies the usual process that requires applicants to be interviewed in person by the extension officer.

passportValidity.text: At the interview at the border you must present a passport that is valid for at least six months. Passport cards will not be accepted.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A valid yellow fever vaccination certificate is required from travellers over 1 year of age arriving directly from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, and from travellers who have transited more than 12 hours through an airport in such a country; travellers must be vaccinated at least 10 days before entering The Bahamas. Since January 2014, proof of yellow fever vaccination is no longer required for travellers arriving from Trinidad and Tobago.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for entry to the Bahamas. The UK government says medical treatment is of a good standard but can be expensive, that serious cases are transferred to Nassau or Freeport, or Miami, by air ambulance, and to check before you travel that you have appropriate travel insurance for local treatment or unexpected medical evacuation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Bahamas travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: The Department of Immigration says that during the interview at the border the prospective visitor must possess a valid return ticket or means of departing The Bahamas, and present a completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival

proofOfFunds.text: The Department of Immigration says that, under the Immigration Act, Chapter 191, Section 22, travellers who are not citizens or legal residents must meet prescribed criteria at the border, including having financial means to sustain themselves during the stay (or identifying a local sponsor who will receive them). No official source we could read states an amount.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival

declarations.name: Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card
declarations.text: During the interview at the border, the prospective visitor must present a completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card, a passport that is valid for at least six months, and a valid return ticket or means of departing The Bahamas. The Department of Immigration asks passengers arriving by sea to complete the Inward Passenger and Crew Manifest for all individuals aboard the vessel.

source.name: Bahamas Department of Immigration — Before Your Arrival

currencyLimits.text: Bahamas Customs says each person or responsible family member travelling is required to declare if they are travelling with cash or negotiable instruments, or precious metals or precious stones, of a value equivalent to BSD 10,000. Penalties for non-compliance can include forfeiture of the cash, plus a fine of up to $2,000.

source.name: Bahamas Customs Department — travellers currency declaration

alsoStatedOn.name: Bahamas Customs Department — Prohibited and restricted imports ("Firearms, fireworks, unless special authorization by the Commissioner of Police")
Bahamas Customs Department — Arriving (USD 100 exemption; spirits, wine and tobacco allowances)

notes: Bahamas Customs lists firearms and fireworks among restricted goods, unless there is special authorization by the Commissioner of Police.

Bahamas Customs says all visitors are entitled to an exemption of $100 on any dutiable article brought into the Bahamas; above that, the necessary customs duties and taxes apply. Duty-free allowances for all travellers: alcoholic beverages not exceeding one quart of spirits and one quart of wine, and tobacco not exceeding one pound in weight or 200 cigarettes or 50 cigars (adults only).

safety.text: The UK government's travel advice says there have been violent crimes and armed robberies, sometimes fatal, in residential and tourist areas of New Providence and Grand Bahama, and advises not going on foot outside the main tourist areas and beaches, especially alone, avoiding unlit areas and travelling in groups after dusk. It warns never to go into water that has been baited.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Bahamas travel advice: safety and security

alsoStatedOn.name: UK FCDO — Bahamas travel advice: warnings (areas where FCDO advises against travel)
Government of Canada — travel advice and advisories: "Exercise a high degree of caution"

source.name: IEC World Plugs (International Electrotechnical Commission) — plug types, voltage and frequency by location

bestTimeToVisit.text: No official source we could read gives a best time to visit. The UK government's travel advice says the hurricane season in The Bahamas normally runs from 1 June to 30 November.

idp.text: The Bahamas is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). The Bahamas' Motor Car (International Circulation) Order, published by the Road Traffic Department, says the holder of an International Driving Permit issued abroad under a convention The Bahamas has adhered to is exempt from holding a Bahamian driver's licence while the permit remains valid. No official source we could read states for how long a visitor may drive on a foreign licence.

source.instrument: Convention on Road Traffic, Vienna, 8 November 1968 (UNTS vol. 1042, p. 17)

driving.text: The Bahamas is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic (UN Treaty Collection). The Bahamas' Motor Car (International Circulation) Order, published by the Road Traffic Department, says the holder of an International Driving Permit issued abroad under a convention The Bahamas has adhered to is exempt from holding a Bahamian driver's licence while the permit remains valid. No official source we could read states for how long a visitor may drive on a foreign licence.

tips.text: The UK government's travel advice says the hurricane season in The Bahamas normally runs from 1 June to 30 November, and that the Government of The Bahamas issues wireless emergency alerts directly to mobile phones and provides updates on the Bahamas Department of Meteorology website. Canada's travel advice says to follow the advice and instructions of local authorities.
Bahamas Customs lists firearms and fireworks among restricted goods, unless there is special authorization by the Commissioner of Police.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for The Bahamas?
faq.answer: The Department of Immigration says Bahamian visa requirements are waived, under official international visa agreements, for citizens of the countries it lists, among them the United Kingdom, the United States of America and Canada, for visits of no more than three or eight months, as each individual agreement may dictate. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists Benin and Ghana among the countries that do not need a visa, and Bosnia among those that do. Citizens of the countries on the Department's visa list must apply for and obtain Bahamian visas before attempting entry.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a passport for The Bahamas?
faq.answer: Yes. The Department of Immigration says that at the interview at the border a prospective visitor must present a passport that is valid for at least six months, and that passport cards will not be accepted.

faq.question: Do I have to fill in a form before arriving?
faq.answer: Yes. The Department of Immigration says the prospective visitor must present a completed Bahamas Immigration Disembarkation/Embarkation Card at the border interview, and asks passengers arriving by sea to complete the Inward Passenger and Crew Manifest for all individuals aboard the vessel.

faq.question: How long can I stay in The Bahamas?
faq.answer: The Department of Immigration says visa waivers allow visits of no more than three or eight months, as each individual agreement may dictate; Canada's travel advice says Canadians do not need a tourist visa for stays of up to 8 months. If you want to stay beyond the period granted, you can apply for a visitor extension before the time granted expires, at the Department's discretion; a non-refundable processing fee of $200 applies to every extension of stay application.

faq.question: Can I work remotely from The Bahamas?
faq.answer: No official source we could read describes a remote-work visa or permit for The Bahamas. The Department of Immigration says visitors must not intend to engage in any gainful employment while in The Bahamas.

faq.question: How much does a Bahamas visitor visa cost?
faq.answer: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists the single-entry Visitor’s Visa at $160.00; no official source we could read names the currency. The fees are payable at the time of visa application and are non-refundable, by credit or debit card (VISA, MasterCard or American Express only). Multiple-entry visas for 3 months, 6 months or 1 year cost $250, and the applicant must provide copies of three previous successful visas to The Bahamas; a 3-year multiple-entry visa costs $500 and is not available online.

countryFacts.safety.text: There have been violent crimes and armed robberies, sometimes fatal, in residential and tourist areas of New Providence and Grand Bahama.
To reduce your risk, do not go on foot outside the main tourist areas and beaches, especially if you are alone.
Avoid unlit areas, and travel in groups after dusk.
Never go into water that has been baited.
